description: Public edition: Distributed robotic laboratories that propose experiments, run approved procedures, and share validated findings.
body:
Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network. Distributed robotic laboratories that propose experiments, run approved procedures, and share validated findings.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 36 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Intelligence Beyond Today's AI". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Self-driving labs are operating reality (Berkeley, Argonne, Toronto); a distributed network sharing validated findings is emerging.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Distributed robotic laboratories that propose experiments, run approved procedures, and share validated findings.
body:
Known science foundations of Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network.

Self-driving laboratories optimize battery electrolytes, catalysts, and thin films autonomously. The Berkeley Lab's A-Lab synthesizes predicted materials. Cloud labs (Emerald Cloud Lab, Strateos) run experiments remotely. Networking these into a shared-findings research network is the next step.

Key quantity check (Self-driving labs operating worldwide / total chemistry labs): computed ratio 0.0005 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Distributed robotic laboratories that propose experiments, run approved procedures, and share validated findings.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network.

Robotic labs are expensive and domain-specific. Sharing findings needs standardized, trustworthy data formats. Approved procedures still need human safety oversight.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 1.3 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is networked labs vs shared findings at 1.3 orders of magnitude (shared findings larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

title: Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: Distributed robotic laboratories that propose experiments, run approved procedures, and share validated findings.
body:
Unresolved problems for Autonomous AI Research Laboratory Network, in priority order (research burden index 17, 1 blocking):

Safety at network scale (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Cross-lab reproducibility (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

Standardizing validated findings (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
